en: The Apadāna of the Elder Vaṇṇakāra Udakāsanavagga 6 I was a painter of forms, skilled in the art of painting. Seeing the Buddha, the Blessed One, I offered him a painting. Because of that wholesome deed, I have attained this fruit. Having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of suffering. Through the power of that merit, I have become a sage. I was then a dyer of cloth;
at the cetiya, [I offered] bundles of cloth.”
Of various colors and stained with dust.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
whatever color I dyed at that time;
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of giving beautiful things.
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Vaṇṇakāra spoke these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Vaṇṇakāra.
